attempts.summary: Configured a transit path between node1 (VyOS, lan-a router) and node2 (OPNsense, lan-b router) so that node3 (behind node1) can reach node4's HTTP service on TCP/8080 (behind node2), while both routers keep default-deny forward policies for everything else. Discovered the real topology by link-testing unconfigured NICs (node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0 = lan-a, node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 = transit, node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0 = lan-b), then statically addressed lan-a (10.10.1.0/24), lan-b (10.10.2.0/24), and the transit link (10.10.0.0/30). On node1 (VyOS) added interface addresses, a static route to lan-b, and a forward-filter default-drop with only an established/related rule and a specific tcp/8080 lan-a->lan-b accept rule. On node2 (OPNsense) added opt1/opt2 interface assignments via config.xml, a gateway+static route back to lan-a, and a single pf pass rule for tcp/8080 from lan-a to lan-b (default-deny already implicit on new interfaces). Verified curl to node4:8080 returns HTTP 200 from node3, while ping and other ports (22, 8081) are refused. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id/kern.boottime baselines on all four nodes, rebooted each node individually (routers first, then LAN hosts), confirmed changed boot identity on every node, and re-verified config persistence (interfaces, routes, firewall/pf rules) and end-to-end HTTP reachability with continued blocking of all other traffic after each restart.
